faq.q: How much does water or mold damage restoration cost?
faq.a: Most Restoration Royalties jobs run between $250 and $40,000+, depending on the type of loss, the square footage affected, and how far the water, mold, or smoke has spread. A mold inspection is at the low end; a full commercial or condo water loss with rebuild is at the high end. Every assessment is free and the scope is documented in writing — and most of the cost is typically covered by your insurance claim, which we help you document from day one.

Yes. Water and storm damage don't wait for business hours, so neither do we — our flagship line rings 24/7, and the emergency call is never left to voicemail. Call the moment you see standing water, a roof leak, or smoke damage; the faster we extract and dry, the less secondary damage and mold you face.

faq.q: Do you help with insurance claims?
faq.a: Absolutely. From the first visit we document the loss with photos, moisture readings, and a line-item scope so your carrier sees exactly what happened and what restoration requires. We work directly with adjusters throughout the file. (We help you document and present your claim; the coverage decision is always your insurer's.)

We serve all of Miami-Dade and Broward counties, and much of Palm Beach — from Miami, Coral Gables, and Pinecrest up through Fort Lauderdale, Pembroke Pines, and Weston. Every call is geo-tagged by ZIP and routed to the nearest available crew for the fastest possible response.

Yes. Restoration Royalties is a licensed and insured South Florida restoration company, and our crews work to IICRC-grade standards. The Florida license and IICRC certification numbers of record are displayed on our public-facing material.

faq.q: Do you have a Spanish line?
faq.a: Sí. We're a bilingual crew and run a dedicated Spanish route — se habla español. Pick your language at the top of this page and both the site and our concierge respond in it.

faq.q: Do you handle commercial, condo, and HOA properties?
faq.a: Yes. Condos, plazas, offices, and full HOA communities get their own priority line and callback SLA, with large-loss crews for tri-county properties. We coordinate with property managers and boards and can work around your tenants and residents.

faq.q: How fast can you get here after a storm?
faq.a: Roof leaks and storm damage surge our crews automatically on weather alerts. When a South Florida storm passes, emergency tarp and dry-in leads route straight to the nearest crew — often same-day — so a temporary leak doesn't become a moldy ceiling.

We rebuild what was damaged and hand your insurer a fully documented file — property restored, paperwork done.
